///Lamont (friend; DM)-Skinwalker (wereboar) Barbarian ///Matthew (brother)-Human Paladin ///Summer (fiance)-Drow Rogue ///Richard (friend)-Human Sorcerer ///Myself-Goblin Rogue named Murch Ant ///(I will add character names as soon as Murch cares enough to ask them. Also, combat is described with a few key tidbits that occurred; I do not believe anyone wants to read every roll made during the session.)

Given the fact that the Drow and I chose to be Evil characters within a primarily Good and Neutral group, the DM decided to begin play with the majority and allows us to enter the story separately. This is my first written game synopsis and not a lot besides combat occurred with this first session, so please bear with me here:

So this all started after the two portions of our party received a letter from an old friend, Doran, who had asked us to visit her promptly at her home just outside of a gritty township. Of course, the 'goody-tushu' PCs knew exactly how to get there, but Murch often forgets things and our Drow cannot communicate in common, and, alas, also cannot remember how to get to their desired location; and of course, the DM had intricately placed a secret objective for the Evil charcacters: we are to find a relic named the Coat of Eyes.

Murch attempts to prod at bystanders, rudely asking them how his 'colleague' and he would make their way to Doran's home, but none of the NPCs would even come near him because of how annoying he was; the Drow is shaking her head in disappointment because, though she does not speak common, she knows that Murch is being an idiot in some way or another (in this case, it was because he was speaking.) We eventually find an NPC who could point us in the right direction, so we headed to our friend's home.

Without trouble we arrived at the home, only to hear individuals already inside (these being the Sorcerer, Barbarian, and Paladin.) Murch knocks on the door and the Sorcerer answers, and in the most annoying voice possible says hi. The Sorcerer slammed the door in Murch's face, then, when asked who knocked, simply stated, "It was no-one;" the jerk then locked the door! Luckily, Murch was able to sneak past the Paladin, who was currently inspecting a blood trail leading out, and invited himself in. The Sorcerer, Barbarian, and-eventually-the Paladin looked shocked at this little Goblin, who waddled up to the door and unlocked it to allow his Drow counterpart inside.

After some assuring of who was who and what aspirations everyone had for being present, the Sorcerer pulled out a pendant with an eye, to which the Drow attempted to steal from right in front of him. After a deadlocked tug-'o-war and Murch deciding to jump at the pendant hanging from the two normal-sized individuals fighting, the chain snapped. The Sorcerer caught it before Murch could, but the Barbarian simply chuckled at all of the foolishness, and eventually he and the Paladin directed everyone toward the blood trail.

A short walk-silent barring Murch's being bored and consistently mistaking the Skinwalker to be an Orc due to him having tusks-the party found itself at the mouth of a cave with two orc guards standing watch just outside. After being denied access to enter, Murch pulls out his shortbow (to which he only has ten common arrows and one barbed arrow) while a dagger was thrown from a tree to symbolize the beginning of combat. In this endeavor, there were four enemies: the two previously mentioned orcs and two dagger-throwers in nearby trees.

The Sorcerer casts a sleep spell at near the Drow and one of the Orcs (which, of course, only affects the Orc since Drow have immunity to magic sleep), rendering the enemy combatant unconscious for an easy elimination by the Paladin. Soon after, the other Orc knocks the Drow out. What the DM-who is completely new to DMing, this being his first game-failed to mention was that the Orcs had a +6 to attack and damage, rendering them nearly unstoppable.

Combat slowed significantly after these occurrences, but the Barbarian eventually climbed into a tree to slaughter a dagger-thrower with his greataxe before focusing on the other Orc. After some time the Paladin is taken out, and it is at this time that Murch, who was hiding in some nearby bushes and taking pot-shots at the dagger-throwers-crawled onto the battlefield and began tying the shoelaces of the Orc combatant, subsequently forcing him to stay down. Murch took a few nasty blows to the ribs by the Orcs, but the Sorcerer, Barbarian, and he were eventually able to take out the last of the resistance before reviving and healing the fallen party members.

We proceeded toward the cave and found strange crimson symbols flowing across the wall. The Paladin attempts to make a Knowledge (Religion) check on the wall but takes some serious mental damage because of how damaging the symbols were. There is a small rest area ahead, which is where we decided to end the session due to a great amount of time being spent out-of-game already.

I hope I can continue to post these up for you all to check out, and I apologize if my grammar is a little off; it's 4:46a here and I need to get up at a decent time tomorrow, having not received much sleep yesterday.
